abstract:
As genome resources continue to expand, estimating the accuracy and completeness of genome annotations (e.g., gene and protein models) becomes essential to ensure quality of downstream analyses and applications. It becomes critical in comparative genomic analysis to select genomes with comparable qualities of assembly and annotation. Without careful scrutiny, inconsistencies in annotation quality can undermine downstream studies.
We have developed Accuracy-Based Annotation Quality Score (ABAQS), a novel method to comprehensively assess genome annotation quality. ABAQS evaluates multiple factors, including genome completeness, gene model validity, and protein profile accuracy, providing a more complete picture of annotation quality than metrics like BUSCO and PSAURON. We applied ABAQS to 1700+ eukaryotic fungal and algal genomes and showed its robustness and effectiveness in evaluating genome annotation quality, making it a valuable tool for researchers working with genomic data.
ABAQS software is available at https://github.com/mycocosm-lbl/abaqs. It requires Java SDK version > =21 and Maven. We also provide a Docker image on DockerHub.
Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
